## Segmentation

### Setup

```{python}

# load data
email = pl.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/numktg/data/main/email.csv")


# Select relevant features for clustering
email_bases = email.select([
    'avg_distance',
    'n_purchase',
    'discount_purchase',
    'n_reward',
    'avg_npassengers',
    'avg_price'])


# Create KMeans pipeline

def create_pipeline(num_clusters, random_seed = 42):
    """
    Creates a machine learning pipeline with a scaler and KMeans.
    """
    pipeline = Pipeline([
        ('scaler', StandardScaler()),
        ('kmeans', KMeans(n_clusters=num_clusters, random_state=random_seed))
    ])
    return pipeline


# Make elbow plot

def calculate_totwithinss(data, k):
    kmeans_pipeline = create_pipeline(k, random_seed=10)
    kmeans_pipeline.fit(data)
    return kmeans_pipeline['kmeans'].inertia_

# Calculate tot.withinss for different values of k
k_values = range(1, 10)
totwithinss_values = [calculate_totwithinss(email_bases, k) for k in k_values]

# Create a DataFrame for results
kmeans_results = pl.DataFrame(
    {'num_clusters': k_values,
     'tot_withinss': totwithinss_values})

# Plot the elbow method using Plotly Express
elbow_plot = px.line(
    data_frame = kmeans_results,
    x = 'num_clusters',
    y = 'tot_withinss', 
    markers = True,
    labels = {
        'num_clusters': 'Number of Clusters', 'tot_withinss': 'Total Within SS'
        },
    title = 'Elbow Method for Optimal k')

elbow_plot.show()

```

### Run k-means analysis on email data

```{python}


# Choose the number of clusters based on the elbow method
optimal_k = 3

# Run K-means clustering

email_kmeans_pipeline = create_pipeline(optimal_k)
email_kmeans_pipeline.fit(email_bases)


# Add cluster assignments to the original data
email_with_clusters = email.with_columns(
    pl.Series(
        "segment_number",
        email_kmeans_pipeline['kmeans'].labels_ + 1
        ).cast(pl.Utf8).cast(pl.Categorical)  # Make cluster labels 1-indexed
)



# Describe segments


segment_summary = email_with_clusters.group_by('segment_number').agg(
    [
        pl.mean('age').alias('mean_age'),
        pl.mean('avg_price').alias('mean_avg_price'),
        pl.mean('avg_distance').alias('mean_avg_distance'),
        pl.len().alias('n')
    ]
)

segment_summary



```


## Targeting and Classification

```{python}

# Load demographic data
demo = pl.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/numktg/data/main/email_demo.csv")

# Combine email and demo data using a left join
# Note! This is only necessary for my example data. If your data already contains all necessarily columns, this step can be skipped
email_joined = email_with_clusters.join(demo, on='ID', how='left')

# Convert to Pandas DataFrame for easier handling with sklearn
email_df = email_joined.to_pandas()

# Encode the target variable using LabelEncoder
label_encoder = LabelEncoder()

email_df['segment_number'] = label_encoder.fit_transform(email_joined['segment_number'])

# Define features and target
features = ['age', 'Education', 'Income', 'Marital_Status', 'Occupation', 'Children', 'Region', 'Gender']
target = 'segment_number'



# Data Splitting

train, test = train_test_split(email_df, test_size=0.3, random_state=101)


# Define column transformer for one-hot encoding categorical features
categorical_features = ['Education', 'Marital_Status', 'Occupation', 'Region', 'Gender', 'Income']
numeric_features = ['age', 'Children']

preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        ('num', 'passthrough', numeric_features),
        ('cat', OneHotEncoder(), categorical_features)
    ]
)
```


### Create Pipeline and Train Model

```{python}

logit_model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, solver='lbfgs')

pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[
        ('preprocessor', preprocessor),
        ('classifier', logit_model)
])
    
# Fit the pipeline on training data
pipeline.fit(train[features], train[target])


# Use trained model to predict test set data
# Note: you use the predict function to predict future/unseen data
# Note: for prediction to work, the data to be predicted needs to contain all features used in the model
test['pred_seg'] = pipeline.predict(test[features])


# Create confusion matrix and compute accuracy
conf_matrix = confusion_matrix(test[target], test['pred_seg'])
accuracy = accuracy_score(test[target], test['pred_seg'])


# Print results
print(f"\nModel: Logistic regression")
print("Confusion Matrix:\n", conf_matrix)
print("Accuracy:", accuracy)

```


## RFM and Feature Engineering

```{python}

# Load dataset
# Download the following two files from google drives, and then drag and drop them into your codespace.

observation_data = pl.read_csv("./customer_observation.csv", ignore_errors = True)

purchaser = pl.read_csv("./customer_outcome.csv", ignore_errors = True)


# Generate R, F, M columns
observation = (observation_data
    .group_by("Customer.ID")
    .agg([
        pl.len().alias("number_of_transactions"),
        pl.sum("Total").alias("total_revenue"),
        pl.min("days_since").alias("most_recent_transaction")
    ])
)

# Visualize these columns

R_hist = px.histogram(observation, x = 'most_recent_transaction')
R_hist.show()


F_hist = px.histogram(observation, x = 'number_of_transactions')
F_hist.show()



M_hist = px.histogram(observation, x = 'total_revenue')
M_hist.show()


# Log-transform for left-skewed distributions
observation_transformed = observation.with_columns([
    pl.col("total_revenue").log().alias("log_total_revenue"),
    pl.col("number_of_transactions").log().alias("log_number_of_transactions"),
])


# Visualize the transformed columns

F_trans_hist = px.histogram(observation_transformed, x = 'log_number_of_transactions')
F_trans_hist.show()



M_trans_hist = px.histogram(observation_transformed, x = 'log_total_revenue')
M_trans_hist.show()

```


### ROMI Formula

- ROMI = Final_Profit / Marketing_Cost
- In the formula above, Final_Profit = Profit - Marketing_Cost



## Continuous Prediction

```{python}

# Load the dataset
data_url = "https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1a6aCUfO0Xw0QEdzT66T4W6VQYCSl_Kzs"
data = pl.read_csv(data_url).drop("") # Removing unnecessary column



# Define features and target
features = [col for col in data.columns if col not in ["id", "purchase_amount"]]
target = "purchase_amount"

# Define preprocessor
categorical_features = []  # Specify if there are any categorical features
numeric_features = features

preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        ('num', StandardScaler(), numeric_features),  # Standard scale numeric features
        ('cat', OneHotEncoder(), categorical_features)  # One-hot encode categorical features
    ]
)

# Split the data into training and testing sets
train, test = train_test_split(data, test_size=0.5, random_state=11109)

train_df = train.to_pandas()
test_df = test.to_pandas()


# Define a linear regression pipeline

lr_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', preprocessor),
    ('model', LinearRegression())
])



# Train and predict
lr_pipeline.fit(train_df[features], train_df[target])
train_df["lr_prediction"] = lr_pipeline.predict(train_df[features])
test_df["lr_prediction"] = lr_pipeline.predict(test_df[features])



# Compute error and RMSE

# Add error columns directly to test dataframe
test_df = pl.DataFrame(test_df).with_columns([
    (pl.col("lr_prediction") - pl.col(target)).alias("lr_error")
])

rmse = test_df.select([
    pl.col("lr_error").pow(2).mean().sqrt().alias("lr_rmse")
])
print("RMSE is:")
print(rmse)

```

## Marketing Mix Modeling Example

```{python}

# Marketing Mix Model Example
marketing_url = "https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=15UaT_hXyPQ5y_jVzkIAiEik6f-IrV51l"
marketing = pd.read_csv(marketing_url)


feature_mmm = ["youtube", "facebook", "newspaper"]
target_mmm = 'sales'



marketing_lr_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ("lr", LinearRegression())
])

marketing_lr_pipeline.fit(marketing[feature_mmm], marketing[target_mmm])

# Display model coefficients
coefficients = marketing_lr_pipeline.named_steps["lr"].coef_

coef_df = pl.DataFrame({
    "Feature": ["youtube", "facebook", "newspaper"],
    "Coefficient": coefficients
})
print("Marketing Mix Model Coefficients:")
print(coef_df)




```

## Association Rules

### Prepare data
```{python}

dataset = [['Milk', 'Onion', 'Nutmeg', 'Kidney Beans', 'Eggs', 'Yogurt'],
           ['Dill', 'Onion', 'Nutmeg', 'Kidney Beans', 'Eggs', 'Yogurt'],
           ['Milk', 'Apple', 'Kidney Beans', 'Eggs'],
           ['Milk', 'Unicorn', 'Corn', 'Kidney Beans', 'Yogurt'],
           ['Corn', 'Onion', 'Onion', 'Kidney Beans', 'Ice cream', 'Eggs']]


te = TransactionEncoder()
te_ary = te.fit(dataset).transform(dataset)

df = pd.DataFrame(te_ary, columns=te.columns_)
df
```

### Compute support through apriori
```{python}
frequent_itemsets = apriori(df, min_support=0.6, use_colnames=True)
frequent_itemsets
```

### Generate association rules results
```{python}
rules = association_rules(frequent_itemsets, metric="lift", min_threshold=0.3)
rules

rules_sorted = rules.sort_values("lift", ascending = False)
rules_sorted # make sure you understand how to interpret antecedent support, consequent support, support, confidence, lift

```
